The schedule doesn't record which subcontractor is responsible for any activity, so I can't say who caused the delay. To answer that, you'd need the activity codes matched to subcontract packages, for example through an activity code or resource assignment in P6.

What the schedule does show is that project completion (#MS-COMPLETE) has slipped +65 working days. Nearly all of that delay comes from longer durations on Phase 7, section 2 activities on the driving path:

| Activity | Name | Added delay |
|---|---|---|
| #P07-A002-STN-0100 | Excavate platform edge, section 2 | +18 days |
| #P07-A002-OLE-0050 | Test cable troughing, section 2 | +12 days |
| #P07-A002-OLE-0220 | Excavate platform edge, section 2 | +12 days |
| #P07-A002-TEL-0140 | Set out mast foundations, section 2 | +11 days |
| #P07-A002-SIG-0190 | Erect cable troughing, section 2 | +9 days |
| #P05-A005-ENB-0200 | Install points machine, section 5 | +5 days |
| #P06-A009-ENB-0120 | Set out sleepers, section 9 | +2 days |

The codes span several disciplines (stations, overhead line equipment (OLE), telecoms, signalling and ENB), so the delay probably sits with more than one party.

The largest single increase may be a data-entry error: #P07-A002-STN-0100 went from 2 to 20 working days and hasn't started yet, so it's worth checking before anyone is held responsible.
